positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described a shocking experience where they thought they might not survive. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reports vivid memories and dreams about the event, feeling panic. Criterion B2 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient actively avoids thoughts and reminders of the event. Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids people and places that trigger memories. Criterion C1 (inability to recall details): MET — patient struggles to remember certain details of the trauma. Criterion C2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient expresses overwhelming negative thoughts about themselves and the world. Criterion C3 (blame): MET — patient blames themselves for not preventing the event. Criterion C4 (negative emotions): MET — patient reports persistent feelings of fear and anger. Criterion C5 (diminished interest): MET — patient has lost interest in activities they once enjoyed. Criterion C6 (detachment): MET — patient feels disconnected from others. Criterion C7 (inability to feel positive emotions): MET — patient finds it hard to experience happiness. Criterion D1 (irritability): MET — patient reports increased irritability and anger outbursts. Criterion D2 (recklessness): MET — patient engages in risky behaviors to escape tension. Criterion D3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient feels constantly on guard and anxious. Criterion D4 (startle response): MET — patient is more easily startled. Criterion D5 (concentration): MET — patient struggles to concentrate. Criterion D6 (sleep disturbance): MET — patient has difficulty sleeping. Criterion E (duration): MET — symptoms began after the traumatic event and have lasted over a month. Criterion F (functional impairment): MET — patient reports significant distress and interference with work and social life. Total: 14 of 14 criteria met (threshold ≥ 1). Exclusions: not triggered; symptoms are consistent with the traumatic event and not due to substances or medical conditions. Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD are met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
